props.title: The Last Legion
props.initialSlug: Roman warrior leads quest to save young emperor

sections.content: **The Last Legion** (2007) represents one of the more peculiar attempts to blend Roman historical epic with Arthurian legend. Following the path carved by **Gladiator** (2000), but lacking its gravitas, the film tries to bridge the gap between the fall of Rome and medieval mythology. It shares DNA with **King Arthur** (2004), which similarly attempted to ground Arthurian legend in Roman history, though with a grimmer tone. Colin Firth's performance as Aurelius feels oddly contemporary, much like how **First Knight** (1995) positioned Richard Gere as an anachronistically modern Lancelot.

sections.content: The film's greatest weakness lies in its uncertain tone, wavering between serious historical drama and fantasy adventure. This tonal confusion echoes similar issues in **Centurion** (2010) and **The Eagle** (2011), both of which tried to ground Roman Britain in a more realistic setting. Director Doug Lefler, coming from television, struggles to achieve the epic scope that Ridley Scott brought to **Kingdom of Heaven** (2005) or what Wolfgang Petersen achieved with **Troy** (2004).

The integration of Excalibur's origin story feels forced, unlike the organic myth-building in **Excalibur** (1981). The film's attempt to connect Roman history with Arthurian legend stumbles where **King Arthur** (2004) at least committed to its historical revisionism. The production values, while adequate, pale compared to HBO's **Rome** (2005-2007) series, which set a new standard for depicting the ancient world on screen. sections.content: **The Last Legion** arrived during a period when the sword-and-sandal genre was struggling to recapture the success of **Gladiator**. Films like **Alexander** (2004) and **Kingdom of Heaven** (2005) proved that even massive budgets and star power couldn't guarantee success. The genre wouldn't see another significant hit until **300** (2007), which took a radically different stylistic approach to ancient warfare.
